1.name: Bulbasaur
1.flavor_text: While it is young, it uses the nutrients that are stored in the seed on its back in order to grow.

2.name: Ivysaur
2.flavor_text: Exposure to sunlight adds to its strength. Sunlight also makes the bud on its back grow larger.

3.name: Venusaur
3.flavor_text: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

4.name: Charmander
4.flavor_text: From the time it is born, a flame burns at the tip of its tail. Its life would end if the flame were to go out.

5.name: Charmeleon
5.flavor_text: If it becomes agitated during battle, it spouts intense flames, incinerating its surroundings.

6.name: Charizard
6.flavor_text: Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.

7.name: Squirtle
7.flavor_text: When it feels threatened, it draws its limbs inside its shell and sprays water from its mouth.

8.name: Wartortle
8.flavor_text: It cleverly controls its furry ears and tail to maintain its balance while swimming.

9.name: Blastoise
9.flavor_text: The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.

10.name: Caterpie
10.flavor_text: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.

11.name: Metapod
11.flavor_text: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can’t withstand a harsh attack.

12.name: Butterfree
12.flavor_text: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.

13.name: Weedle
13.flavor_text: Beware of the sharp stinger on its head. It hides in grass and bushes where it eats leaves.

14.name: Kakuna
14.flavor_text: Able to move only slightly. When endangered, it may stick out its stinger and poison its enemy.

15.name: Beedrill
15.flavor_text: It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.

16.name: Pidgey
16.flavor_text: Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.

17.name: Pidgeotto
17.flavor_text: This Pokémon is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.

18.name: Pidgeot
18.flavor_text: This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.

19.name: Rattata
19.flavor_text: Will chew on anything with its fangs. If you see one, you can be certain that 40 more live in the area.

20.name: Raticate
20.flavor_text: Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.

21.name: Spearow
21.flavor_text: Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its territory.

22.name: Fearow
22.flavor_text: A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.

23.name: Ekans
23.flavor_text: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

24.name: Arbok
24.flavor_text: The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.

25.name: Pikachu
25.flavor_text: Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.

26.name: Raichu
26.flavor_text: It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.

27.name: Sandshrew
27.flavor_text: It burrows into the ground to create its nest. If hard stones impede its tunneling, it uses its sharp claws to shatter them and then carries on digging.

28.name: Sandslash
28.flavor_text: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.

29.name: Nidoran F
29.flavor_text: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran’s horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male’s horn.

30.name: Nidorina
30.flavor_text: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.

31.name: Nidoqueen
31.flavor_text: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.

32.name: Nidoran M
32.flavor_text: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it’s friendly with.

33.name: Nidorino
33.flavor_text: It’s nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.

34.name: Nidoking
34.flavor_text: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.

35.name: Clefairy
35.flavor_text: It can be found in quiet mountain areas on a full moon's night. Its dancing and its tiny, faintly glowing wings confer upon it a lovely fairylike quality.

36.name: Clefable
36.flavor_text: Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.

37.name: Vulpix
37.flavor_text: In its belly burns a fire, which Vulpix spits out in the form of fireballs. When young, this Pokémon has but one white tail. As the Pokémon matures, this single tail splits into six.

38.name: Ninetales
38.flavor_text: The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.

39.name: Jigglypuff
39.flavor_text: By freely changing the wavelength of its voice, Jigglypuff sings a mysterious melody sure to make any listener sleepy.

40.name: Wigglytuff
40.flavor_text: It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.

41.name: Zubat
41.flavor_text: Makes its home in gloomy caves. Atrophied eyes have left this Pokémon blind, so it scans its surroundings via sound waves that it emits from its mouth as it flies.

42.name: Golbat
42.flavor_text: It sinks its sharp fangs into other creatures and slurps up their blood. A closer look at the fangs reveals that they are hollow and akin to straws.

43.name: Oddish
43.flavor_text: During the day, it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun. It grows by bathing in moonlight.

44.name: Gloom
44.flavor_text: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.

45.name: Vileplume
45.flavor_text: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.

46.name: Paras
46.flavor_text: Sometimes seen at the foot of trees in humid forests. The mushrooms on its back—called tochukaso—are not present on infant specimens and instead emerge as Paras matures.

47.name: Parasect
47.flavor_text: Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.

48.name: Venonat
48.flavor_text: Its large eyes act as radar. In a bright place, you can see that they are clusters of many tiny eyes.

49.name: Venomoth
49.flavor_text: The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove from skin. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.

50.name: Diglett
50.flavor_text: It burrows through the ground at a shallow depth. It leaves raised earth in its wake, making it easy to spot.

51.name: Dugtrio
51.flavor_text: These Diglett triplets dig over 60 miles below sea level. No one knows what it’s like underground.

52.name: Meowth
52.flavor_text: It washes its face regularly to keep the coin on its forehead spotless. It doesn’t get along with Galarian Meowth.

53.name: Persian
53.flavor_text: Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.

54.name: Psyduck
54.flavor_text: Suffers perpetual headaches. If the agony grows too great, Psyduck's latent power erupts, contrary to Psyduck's intent. Ergo, I am exploring ways to ease the pain.

55.name: Golduck
55.flavor_text: Its body is strong, and it has webbing on its hands and feet. Golduck can swim easily through rough seas, clawing its way through the high waves.

56.name: Mankey
56.flavor_text: An agile Pokémon that lives in trees. It angers easily and will not hesitate to attack anything.

57.name: Primeape
57.flavor_text: It stops being angry only when nobody else is around. To view this moment is very difficult.

58.name: Growlithe
58.flavor_text: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

59.name: Arcanine
59.flavor_text: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

60.name: Poliwag
60.flavor_text: In rivers with fast-flowing water, this Pokémon will cling to a rock by using its thick lips, which act like a suction cup.

61.name: Poliwhirl
61.flavor_text: This Pokémon’s sweat is a slimy mucus. When captured, Poliwhirl can slither from its enemies’ grasp and escape.

62.name: Poliwrath
62.flavor_text: Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.

63.name: Abra
63.flavor_text: Spends 18 hours of the day sleeping. Even while asleep, Abra can control its psychic powers—should danger approach, the Pokémon will simply teleport away.

64.name: Kadabra
64.flavor_text: There are rumors that a child with mystical powers became a Kadabra; however, this remains unverified. I suspect that the spoon Kadabra holds enhances its brain waves.

65.name: Alakazam
65.flavor_text: The longer Alakazam lives, the larger and heavier its head becomes. Our tests have shown that the strength of its psychic powers correlates positively to the weight of its head.

66.name: Machop
66.flavor_text: Though as small as a child, it has strength enough to easily throw a well-built adult. Striving to become ever stronger, Machop trains by carrying a Graveler on its shoulders.

67.name: Machoke
67.flavor_text: A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.

68.name: Machamp
68.flavor_text: In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.

69.name: Bellsprout
69.flavor_text: Prefers hot and humid places. It ensnares tiny bugs with its vines and devours them.

70.name: Weepinbell
70.flavor_text: When hungry, it swallows anything that moves. Its hapless prey is dissolved by strong acids.

71.name: Victreebel
71.flavor_text: Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is dissolved in a day, bones and all.

72.name: Tentacool
72.flavor_text: They fire beams from the glassy, magenta orbs that resemble eyes atop their heads, and they drift in shallow seas. During low tide, they can sometimes be found on beaches, desiccated.

73.name: Tentacruel
73.flavor_text: It has 80 tentacles, each with a venomous tip. These tentacles are also extendible, lengthening when Tentacruel attempts to catch prey. Use caution.

74.name: Geodude
74.flavor_text: Makes its home in mountainous regions, using its arms to climb along harsh mountain roads. Can be troublesome—carelessly kicking one will cause it to fly into a rage and chase after you.

75.name: Graveler
75.flavor_text: Dwells in holes dug into sheer walls of stone. It enjoys rolling down slopes as though it were a boulder during a rockfall, so keep an eye upward while traversing mountain roads.

76.name: Golem
76.flavor_text: The rocklike shell is shed each year. The cast-off shell then crumbles, reverting to a mass of soil, which can be spread across fields to promote crop growth.

77.name: Ponyta
77.flavor_text: These Pokémon live in herds out in the grassland. Newborn foals lack their fiery manes, which will develop about an hour after birth.

78.name: Rapidash
78.flavor_text: Fiery mane aglow, Rapidash darts like an arrow across the land. This prodigiously swift creature can traverse the vast region of Hisui in a day and a half.

79.name: Slowpoke
79.flavor_text: When this Pokémon’s tail is soaked in water, sweetness seeps from it. Slowpoke uses this trait to lure in and fish up other Pokémon.

80.name: Slowbro
80.flavor_text: Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.

81.name: Magnemite
81.flavor_text: A bizarre Pokémon with but a single eye embedded in an iron sphere. I suspect this creature levitates due to the magnetism it emits from its arms, which resemble horseshoe-shaped magnets.

82.name: Magneton
82.flavor_text: Three Magnemite gathered to evolve into this Pokémon. The source of much vexation on my part, as its powerful magnetism destroys my research equipment.

83.name: Farfetchd
83.flavor_text: They use a plant stalk as a weapon, but not all of them use it in the same way. Several distinct styles of stalk fighting have been observed.

84.name: Doduo
84.flavor_text: Its short wings make flying difficult. Instead, this Pokémon runs at high speed on developed legs.

85.name: Dodrio
85.flavor_text: One of Doduo’s two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.

86.name: Seel
86.flavor_text: Loves freezing-cold conditions. Relishes swimming in a frigid climate of around 14 degrees Fahrenheit.

87.name: Dewgong
87.flavor_text: Its entire body is a snowy white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.

88.name: Grimer
88.flavor_text: Made of congealed sludge. It smells too putrid to touch. Even weeds won’t grow in its path.

89.name: Muk
89.flavor_text: Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration of its nose, it lost its sense of smell.

90.name: Shellder
90.flavor_text: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.

91.name: Cloyster
91.flavor_text: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.

92.name: Gastly
92.flavor_text: Gaseous and completely impalpable. Also highly dangerous— inhaling part of its poisonous body will cause one to faint instantly.

93.name: Haunter
93.flavor_text: This frightful, malevolent spirit can glide through walls, appearing wherever it likes. According to rumor, victims of a Haunter's lick will wither to death day by day.

94.name: Gengar
94.flavor_text: Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!

95.name: Onix
95.flavor_text: This chain of immense stones resembles a giant serpent. Tremors shake the earth above as it burrows deep beneath the ground, feeding on boulders as it goes.

96.name: Drowzee
96.flavor_text: If you sleep by it all the time, it will sometimes show you dreams it had eaten in the past.

97.name: Hypno
97.flavor_text: Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.

98.name: Krabby
98.flavor_text: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.

99.name: Kingler
99.flavor_text: Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.

100.name: Voltorb
100.flavor_text: An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.

101.name: Electrode
101.flavor_text: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.

102.name: Exeggcute
102.flavor_text: These Pokémon get nervous when they’re not in a group of six. The minute even one member of the group goes missing, Exeggcute become cowardly.

103.name: Exeggutor
103.flavor_text: When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.

104.name: Cubone
104.flavor_text: This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased mother. Sometimes Cubone’s dreams make it cry, but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.

105.name: Marowak
105.flavor_text: When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.

106.name: Hitmonlee
106.flavor_text: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.

107.name: Hitmonchan
107.flavor_text: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.

108.name: Lickitung
108.flavor_text: Wields its long tongue deftly, as though it were an arm. The Pokémon's viscous saliva, once it has been collected and boiled down, yields a strong and highly useful adhesive.

109.name: Koffing
109.flavor_text: It adores polluted air. Some claim that Koffing used to be more plentiful in the Galar region than they are now.

110.name: Weezing
110.flavor_text: It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.

111.name: Rhyhorn
111.flavor_text: Ludicrously strong—when it butts heads with a mountain, it is the mountain that shatters. But its short legs struggle with turns, and it is incapable of stopping unless it collides with something.

112.name: Rhydon
112.flavor_text: Rapidly rotates its horn to bore through bedrock. It swaggers around volcanic regions, protected from the lava's heat by its tough, armorlike hide.

113.name: Chansey
113.flavor_text: This purehearted Pokémon shares its eggs with the injured.

114.name: Tangela
114.flavor_text: It is cloaked entirely in blue vines, preventing any glimpse of its true identity. The vines impart a refreshing sensation when chewed—they're useful as a spice.

115.name: Kangaskhan
115.flavor_text: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.

116.name: Horsea
116.flavor_text: They swim with dance-like motions and cause whirlpools to form. Horsea compete to see which of them can generate the biggest whirlpool.

117.name: Seadra
117.flavor_text: Seadra’s mouth is slender, but its suction power is strong. In an instant, Seadra can suck in food that’s larger than the opening of its mouth.

118.name: Goldeen
118.flavor_text: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.

119.name: Seaking
119.flavor_text: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

120.name: Staryu
120.flavor_text: Fish Pokémon nibble at it, but Staryu isn’t bothered. Its body regenerates quickly, even if part of it is completely torn off.

121.name: Starmie
121.flavor_text: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.

122.name: Mr Mime
122.flavor_text: The behavior of this clown-like Pokémon reminds one of pantomime. It creates invisible walls using a force emitted from its fingertips.

123.name: Scyther
123.flavor_text: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.

124.name: Jynx
124.flavor_text: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.

125.name: Electabuzz
125.flavor_text: Feeds on electrical energy. During sudden showers beneath looming thunderclouds, one can observe Electabuzz scaling tall trees, where the Pokémon will then wait for lightning to strike.

126.name: Magmar
126.flavor_text: Legend has it that this Pokémon was born from the crater of a volcano. When wounded, it bathes in lava to heal its body, much as one would soak in a hot spring.

127.name: Pinsir
127.flavor_text: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.

128.name: Tauros
128.flavor_text: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.

129.name: Magikarp
129.flavor_text: A feeble, pitiful imbecile of a Pokémon that is nonetheless very hardy. Unperturbed by turbid water, it can be found living in all sorts of places.

130.name: Gyarados
130.flavor_text: I suspect this Pokémon to be the true identity of a dragon written of in ancient texts, which claimed that it razed an entire village with white-hot beams from its maw.

131.name: Lapras
131.flavor_text: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.

132.name: Ditto
132.flavor_text: When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.

133.name: Eevee
133.flavor_text: Harbors the potential to evolve into manifold forms. Within Eevee lies the key to the mysteries of Pokémon evolution—I'm certain of it.

134.name: Vaporeon
134.flavor_text: Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.

135.name: Jolteon
135.flavor_text: Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.

136.name: Flareon
136.flavor_text: Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

137.name: Porygon
137.flavor_text: It has no discernible heartbeat and does not seem to draw breath, and yet it appears to function without issue. I cannot even begin to explain this utterly bizarre anomaly.

138.name: Omanyte
138.flavor_text: This Pokémon is a member of an ancient, extinct species. Omanyte paddles through water with its 10 tentacles, looking like it’s just drifting along.

139.name: Omastar
139.flavor_text: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.

140.name: Kabuto
140.flavor_text: While some say this species has gone extinct, Kabuto sightings are apparently fairly common in some places.

141.name: Kabutops
141.flavor_text: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.

142.name: Aerodactyl
142.flavor_text: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.

143.name: Snorlax
143.flavor_text: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.

144.name: Articuno
144.flavor_text: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.

145.name: Zapdos
145.flavor_text: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.

146.name: Moltres
146.flavor_text: There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.

147.name: Dratini
147.flavor_text: This Pokémon was long considered to be no more than a myth. The small lump on a Dratini’s forehead is actually a horn that’s still coming in.

148.name: Dragonair
148.flavor_text: This Pokémon gathers power in the orbs on its tail and controls the weather. When enshrouded by an aura, Dragonair has a mystical appearance.

149.name: Dragonite
149.flavor_text: This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.

150.name: Mewtwo
150.flavor_text: Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.

151.name: Mew
151.flavor_text: When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.

152.name: Chikorita
152.flavor_text: In battle, Chikorita waves its leaf around to keep the foe at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, becalming the battling Pokémon and creating a cozy, friendly atmosphere all around.

153.name: Bayleef
153.flavor_text: Bayleef’s neck is ringed by curled-up leaves. Inside each tubular leaf is a small shoot of a tree. The fragrance of this shoot makes people peppy.

154.name: Meganium
154.flavor_text: The fragrance of Meganium’s flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe’s fighting spirit.

155.name: Cyndaquil
155.flavor_text: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.

156.name: Quilava
156.flavor_text: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.

157.name: Typhlosion
157.flavor_text: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.

158.name: Totodile
158.flavor_text: Despite the smallness of its body, Totodile’s jaws are very powerful. While the Pokémon may think it is just playfully nipping, its bite has enough power to cause serious injury.

159.name: Croconaw
159.flavor_text: Once Croconaw has clamped its jaws on its foe, it will absolutely not let go. Because the tips of its fangs are forked back like barbed fishhooks, they become impossible to remove when they have sunk in.

160.name: Feraligatr
160.flavor_text: Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.

161.name: Sentret
161.flavor_text: When Sentret sleeps, it does so while another stands guard. The sentry wakes the others at the first sign of danger. When this Pokémon becomes separated from its pack, it becomes incapable of sleep due to fear.

162.name: Furret
162.flavor_text: Furret has a very slim build. When under attack, it can slickly squirm through narrow spaces and get away. In spite of its short limbs, this Pokémon is very nimble and fleet.

163.name: Hoothoot
163.flavor_text: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.

164.name: Noctowl
164.flavor_text: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.

165.name: Ledyba
165.flavor_text: These very cowardly Pokémon join together and use Reflect to protect their nest.

166.name: Ledian
166.flavor_text: It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.

167.name: Spinarak
167.flavor_text: Although the poison from its fangs isn’t that strong, it’s potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.

168.name: Ariados
168.flavor_text: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.

169.name: Crobat
169.flavor_text: Its hind limbs have become another set of wings. Crobat expertly maneuvers its four wings to dart in exquisite fashion through even the most confined caves without losing any speed.

170.name: Chinchou
170.flavor_text: On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.

171.name: Lanturn
171.flavor_text: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.

172.name: Pichu
172.flavor_text: Pichu stores electricity in the sacs on its cheeks but discharges it inadvertently when agitated or excited. Being yet immature, the Pokémon's handling of electricity is rather inept.

173.name: Cleffa
173.flavor_text: In silhouette, they resemble twinkling starlight. When shooting stars rain from the night sky, Cleffa gather in numbers and dance as though they are indeed incarnations of the stars.

174.name: Igglybuff
174.flavor_text: Taking advantage of the softness of its body, Igglybuff moves as if bouncing. Its body turns a deep pink when its temperature rises.

175.name: Togepi
175.flavor_text: This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.

176.name: Togetic
176.flavor_text: No records exist of Togetic being seen in the wilds. Rumors abound that it evolves under the loving care of a trusted human companion, upon whom the Pokémon then bestows great joy.

177.name: Natu
177.flavor_text: Because its wings aren’t yet fully grown, it has to hop to get around. It is always staring at something.

178.name: Xatu
178.flavor_text: This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.

179.name: Mareep
179.flavor_text: Rubbing its fleece generates electricity. You’ll want to pet it because it’s cute, but if you use your bare hand, you’ll get a painful shock.

180.name: Flaaffy
180.flavor_text: It stores electricity in its fluffy fleece. If it stores up too much, it will start to go bald in those patches.

181.name: Ampharos
181.flavor_text: Its tail shines bright and strong. It has been prized since long ago as a beacon for sailors.

182.name: Bellossom
182.flavor_text: Bellossom gather at times and appear to dance. They say that the dance is a ritual to summon the sun.

183.name: Marill
183.flavor_text: Even after Marill swims in a cold sea, its water- repellent fur dries almost as soon as Marill leaves the water. That’s why this Pokémon is never cold.

184.name: Azumarill
184.flavor_text: These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.

185.name: Sudowoodo
185.flavor_text: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.

186.name: Politoed
186.flavor_text: The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.

187.name: Hoppip
187.flavor_text: This Pokémon drifts and floats with the wind. If it senses the approach of strong winds, Hoppip links its leaves with other Hoppip to prepare against being blown away.

188.name: Skiploom
188.flavor_text: Skiploom’s flower blossoms when the temperature rises above 64 degrees Fahrenheit. How much the flower opens depends on the temperature. For that reason, this Pokémon is sometimes used as a thermometer.

189.name: Jumpluff
189.flavor_text: Jumpluff rides warm southern winds to cross the sea and fly to foreign lands. The Pokémon descends to the ground when it encounters cold air while it is floating.

190.name: Aipom
190.flavor_text: This treetop dweller possesses a tail as dexterous as a hand. Ancient writings describe this Pokémon as a one-armed oddity.
